why: Graded motor imagery is a structured approach sometimes used for particular persistent pain conditions. Evidence and suitability vary.

slides.title: What Is GMI?
slides.content: Graded motor imagery is a sequence of brain- and movement-based tasks that may be considered when ordinary movement feels highly threatening or difficult.

slides.title: The Usual Sequence
slides.content: Programs commonly progress through left/right discrimination, imagined movement, and mirror therapy. The dose and order should be individualized.

slides.title: Evidence Has Limits
slides.content: Research is most established in conditions such as complex regional pain syndrome and phantom-limb pain, but certainty is limited and results do not apply equally to every pain problem.

slides.title: Not a Test of Willpower
slides.content: Difficulty with imagery or laterality does not mean you are failing. A clinician can help decide whether this approach fits your presentation.

slides.title: Discuss Before Practising
slides.content: If this lesson seems relevant, ask your clinician whether a structured GMI program is appropriate instead of assuming it is a universal pain treatment.
